title: Safe Promise Timeout Wrapper
problemStatement: Implement `withTimeout(promise, ms, timeoutErrorMsg)` that returns a Promise that rejects with an Error(`timeoutErrorMsg`) if `promise` does not settle within `ms` milliseconds.
interviewTrap: Not clearing the timer when the primary promise resolves or rejects, leaving open handles in server environments.

testCases.name: Resolves if promise completes before timeout
testCases.testFn: const p = new Promise(r => setTimeout(() => r('fast-result'), 10)); return withTimeout(p, 100);

testCases.name: Rejects with timeout error if operation takes too long
testCases.testFn: const p = new Promise(r => setTimeout(() => r('slow'), 100)); try { await withTimeout(p, 20, 'Timed out!'); return 'FAIL'; } catch (e) { return e.message; }

testCases.name: Preserves original promise rejection
testCases.testFn: const p = Promise.reject(new Error('original-error')); try { await withTimeout(p, 100); return 'FAIL'; } catch (e) { return e.message; }

details.name: Resolves if promise completes before timeout
Rejects with timeout error if operation takes too long

detailedExplanation.conceptualOverview: Network requests or asynchronous operations can hang indefinitely if servers stall. A Safe Promise Timeout Wrapper races an asynchronous promise against a timer promise that rejects with a `TimeoutError` if the specified duration expires first.
stepByStepWalkthrough: Create a timer promise that sets a `setTimeout` to reject with `new Error('Timeout')`.
Use `Promise.race([promise, timerPromise])` to return whichever settles first.
Ensure the timeout timer is cleared via `clearTimeout` when the target promise resolves or rejects to prevent timer resource leaks.
detailedExplanation.underlyingEngineInternals: `Promise.race` attaches `.then()` handlers to all passed promises. Whichever settles first transitions the returned promise into fulfilled or rejected state. Subsequent completions of the other promise are ignored because a Promise can only transition state once (immutability of promise settlement per ECMA-262 §27.2).

complexity.space: O(1) memory for timer and race promise.

edgeCasesHandled: Fast operations resolve before timeout without penalty.
Slow operations reject with timeout error accurately.
Rejections from the target promise propagate immediately without waiting for timeout.
Timer handle is cleared to prevent keeping Node.js event loop alive.

specifications: MDN Web Docs: Promise.race & timeout patterns
verifiedRules: Promise settlement is irreversible once transitioned from pending.
Promise.race settles with the result of the first settled promise.
